claim: El Puerto de Santa María is one of three Sherry Triangle towns with Jerez and Sanlúcar; its tidal-river bodegas give Finos a distinctive salty taste, sold as Puerto Fino.
quote: Since dry Sherries (or Finos) age in contact with the air, the location of the bodegas, right next to a tidal river, gives Finos from el Puerto a very distinctive and slightly salty taste.

claim: Before the Cádiz rail link, all Jerez sherry was stored in El Puerto warehouses before shipping worldwide; local styles include fino (driest, palest), amontillado and oloroso, while manzanilla is exclusive to Sanlúcar.
quote: all the sherry from Jerez was stored in warehouses at Santa Maria before being shipped all over the world

claim: Bodegas Osborne in El Puerto offers a fortified-wine tasting at 12€, a brandy tasting at 15€ and a VORS tasting at 35€ per person, plus a Toro Gallery stroll with four sherries and Cinco Jotas Iberian ham.
quote: Fortified wine tasting: 12€ (per person), Brandy tasting: 15€ (per person), and VORS tasting: 35€ (per person)

claim: Osborne's El Puerto cellar is the oldest aging bodega in the Jerez region, producing Quinta fino, Coquinero amontillado, Bailén and Sibarita oloroso, and Pedro Ximénez 1827, with tastings, a shop and visits at Calle Los Moros 7.
quote: la bodega de envejecimiento más antigua del marco de Jerez

claim: Bodegas Caballero's Castle + Winery experience inside the 13th-century Castillo de San Marcos runs ~2 hours, costs €14-20 adults / €5 children, and tastes three Jerez wines, a Lustau vermouth and the famous Ponche Caballero.
quote: Includes guided castle tour plus tasting of "three excellent Jerez wines, a Lustau vermouth and the famous Ponche Caballero"

claim: Bodegas Gutiérrez Colosía, founded 1838 and the only riverside winery on the Guadalete by the Cádiz ferry, runs 1.5-hour tours ending in a six-wine tasting, with English at 11.15am and Spanish at 12.30pm Mon-Fri.
quote: Tours last 1½ hours and end with a six-wine tasting, which can include tapas and flamenco on request, and run at 11.15am in English and 12.30pm in Spanish Monday to Friday

claim: Bodegas Grant (Juan C. Grant, est. 1841, aka Las 7 Esquinas) is a family producer of Puerto Fino by the criaderas-and-soleras method, with a traditional tasting patio; visits are Saturdays by prior appointment.
quote: Visits are possible on Saturday with previous appointment.

claim: Bodegas 501 (Carlos & Javier de Terry) is a historic El Puerto brandy house behind Brandy 501, but it ceased winery activity to become a distributor and since 2009 its 501 range is produced by Grupo Osborne.
quote: In 2009, a major agreement was reached with Grupo Osborne, by which Osborne would undertake to produce the 501 brandy range in its three varieties for the national market.
